Commentary.Commentary: The Windies bowlers on the other hand, will look to get a wicket or two early and keep the pressure on this fragile batting line-up. The wicket is providing a lot of assistance to the bowlers and it is not going to be easy to bat on it. Let's see how the hosts reply now...

Earlier in the innings, the West Indian top order failed to show any resistance, except for Powell who missed out on a ton by just 10 runs, in spite of getting three lives by Cremer. Raza was the tormentor as he picked up his first fifer in Test cricket. They had the away side down and out at 230-7 but then the partnership between Holder and Dowrich kept them at bay. They were also aided by some really sloppy fielding from the hosts. The Zimbabweans, who will be mentally tired as they were made to toil really hard in the field, will have to come out and bat really well. A lot will depend on their top order if they are to wipe out the deficit. Their first aim will be to bat out the tricky 25-minute period before lunch safely.

A brilliant batting display by the Windies skipper, Jason Holder and Shane Dowrich. Their record 212-run stand has ensured the hosts stretch their lead beyond hundred and are now in a comfortable position. They came out today morning and looked positive throughout. Both got to their respective tons but departed soon after. The Zimbabwean bowlers did bowl well but to no luck. Chisoro was their pick of the bowlers today as he picked all the three wickets to fall.

OUT! THE WINDIES HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 448 AND THEY LEAD BY 122! Chisoro fires in an arm ball on off, Roach plays for the turn but there isn't any. He tries to defend the ball with the bat close to his pads and there is confusion whether it hit the pad first or the bat. The bowler makes a huge appeal and after a while the umpire raises his finger. Roach thinks about a review but there are none left. Replays show that it had brushed the pad before it hit the bat.
Flatter on off, Roach defends it off the front foot.
Gives it air on off, turns away further. Gabriel tries to defend but gets beaten.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Loopy ball on off, the batsman defends it with authority.

FOUR! Where did that come from? Shannon Gabriel says enough of blocking now. Cremer flights it on middle, Gabriel plants his front foot ahead and lofts it over the mid on fielder and it goes on the bounce for a boundary.
Loopy ball on middle, Shannon defends it stoutly.
Floats it full on off, Gabriel defends it solidly.
A similar length ball, turns away sharply. Roach again is beaten on the defense.
Quicker on off, turning away. Roach tries to defend but gets beaten.
Tosses it up outside off, Roach tries to drive but gets an inside edge and the ball goes on the bounce to short leg.
Flatter outside off, Roach need not play at it.
Bowls it outside off, Roach lets it be.
Full toss, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Comes around the wicket and fires it on the pads. Roach tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
Wide enough for the batsman to play at it.
Floats it on off, Roach defends it solidly.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tosses it up on off, Roach tries to defend but is beaten by the away spin.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Shannon Gabriel is the last man in.

OUT! TIMBER! It took Chisoro almost 39 overs to get him his first Test wicket and now he gets another one! He has got both the centurions in this innings. He comes over the wicket and lands it outside leg stump, gets it to turn into the batsman. Holder tries to paddle it but misses and the ball knocks the leg stump apart. A brilliant, brilliant knock by Holder comes to an end. Well played, Jason! Zimbabwe too show great gesture as they shake his hand as he walks off. The Windies lead by 117 runs.
Full and wide outside off, Holder lets it be.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
A googly on middle, Roach tries to defend but gets beaten and is hit on the pads. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Missing leg!
BEATEN! Cremer bowls it slower through the air on off, the ball drifts into the batsman and then turns away sharply. Roach tries to defend but gets beaten.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floats it on off, Roach defends it solidly.
Tosses it up on off, Roach defends it off the front foot.
Flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
Kemar Roach is the next man in.

OUT! Chisoro gets his first Test wicket and he is overwhelmed, not something he will be forgetting soon! He has bowled well and he deserves it. He fires it on leg stump, gets it to straighten. Dowrich tries to sweep but misses to get hit on the front pad. The players appeal and the umpire after giving it a hard thought raises his finger. Dowrich straightaway reviews it. Replays show that there is no inside edge and returns three reds on the Hawk Eye. West Indies also lose a review. Dowrich has to walk back and he does so to a standing ovation by his teammates. He is also being congratulated by the Zimbabwean players. The mammoth 212-run stand has been broken. West Indies now lead by 116.
Review! The umpire finally gives one out but Dowrich has reviewed it. Will Chisoro finally get his first Test wicket? He is already celebrating.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Floats it up on off, Dowrich defends it solidly.
Sweeps the ball hard towards the square leg fielder who makes a good stop diving to his right.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Driven towards the mid on region.
Floats it full outside off, Holder goes for the expansive drive but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
SIX! BANG! Holder gets into the act. He sees the flighted delivery and just lifts it over the extra cover fence for a biggie.
It's been driven superbly through the covers.
Drives it through mid on for a run.

SIX! MAIDEN TEST HUNDRED FOR DOWRICH! What a way to bring it up. A tossed up ball on off, Dowrich lofts it over the long off fence for a maximum. He too roars in joy as soon as he hits it. He walks upto his captain to receive a hug from him. Also this brings up the 200-run stand between the two.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A nice moment there! Graeme Cremer goes upto Holder and congratulates him on reaching his hundred.
Flatter on the pads, Dowrich flicks it through square leg and good running helps them get three.
The ball is down the leg side but the batsman still goes after it.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.

FOUR! Hundred for Holder. His second in Tests. What a moment for him and what a knock it has been from the skipper. He is leading from the front here and look what it means to him. Chisoro tosses it up on off, Holder leans into it and drives it through covers for a boundary. He makes a loud roar as soon as he hits it. He pumps his fist and acknowledges the applause from the dressing room. He is also the first West Indian to make a Test century coming in at no. 9. He knows he still has to continue as the job is yet not done.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Quicker on off, the straighter one by Chisoro. Holder defends it stoutly.

Drinks are on the field. The West Indies batsmen are going great guns and have swelled the lead to almost 100 now. Holder was dropped on 78 by Chakabva. The third new ball also created chances but none of them favored Zimbabwe. Both the batsmen are on the verge of registering their respective tons. Will they start to attack once they reach personal milestones? Remains to be seen...
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.
Works it to mid-wicket with the spin again.
Drives it with the spin through mid on for a run.

ANOTHER HUGE SHOUT! Raza is making things happen here! He fires it on middle, gets it to turn into the batsman. Dowrich tries to work it on the leg side but misses and is struck on the pads. Raza pleads to the umpire but he remains put. The ball once again is missing leg as it has turned too much. The batsmen run a leg bye.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.

BEAUTY! Raza bowls it flatter outside off, goes on with the arm. Dowrich tries to defend but gets beaten. Chakabva behind the stumps fails to collect and the batsmen run a bye. Raza has bowled really well! Alan Wilkins on-air mentions that Raza could have had 7 to 8 wickets in this innings, that is how well he has bowled.

Well done Peter Moor! Shorter in length outside off, Dowrich guides it through point. Moor hares after it and dives to pull it back in. They go upstairs to check whether the stop is clean and yes it is. He has saved a run for his side.

Bowled? Oh no, the noise was of the ball hitting the keeper's pads. But that was agonizingly close to the leg pole. Chisoro fires it down the leg side, turning in. Dowrich goes for the sweep but misses and the ball nearly kisses the leg stump and hits Chakabva low on his pads. The bowler too got excited for a moment there.
Quicker but on the shorter side. Dowrich rocks back and punches it to the man at covers.
Drags his length back outside off, Holder punches it towards cover where Raza dives over the ball and concedes a run.
Tosses it up on middle, Holder defends it towards covers.
Flatter on off, Holder defends it off the back foot.
Tendai Chisoro is into the attack. He is still searching for his first Test wicket.
Floats it up on off, Dowrich lunges forward in defense.
Driven through mid off by the batsman.
Fuller outside off, Dowrich drives it to covers.
Plays it with the spin to mid-wicket.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground. The batsmen have run through for a single.

HUGE SHOUT! Raza tosses it up on off, turns back in. Holder prods forward to defend but misses and is struck on the pads. The bowler appeals but the umpire is not interested. Raza cannot belevie it, he thought that was out. It was missing leg, turned way too much. A good decision there by Simon Fry.
On the shorter side again! Shane defends it onto the ground.
He bends his back this time and bowls a bouncer. A quick one. Dowrich ducks under it.
Comes around the wicket! Time for some short stuff? Oh yes! He bangs it in on leg stump. Comes really slow off the surface, no pace at all. Dowrich jumps and blocks it towards square leg.
Good length outside off, Dowrich guides it towards point.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Fuller in length on middle, Shane drives it to mid on.

That stayed really low! The tall man did really well to play that! Raza fires it on middle, Holder goes back to flick it. The ball stays extremely low and hits the bottom of Holder's bat and goes on the bounce to short leg. Had he missed that was plumb in front. Sings of the pitch wearing?
Dowrich into the 90s now! Flatter outside off, Dowrich pushes it towards covers for a run.
Fuller in length outside off, the spin is out of the question here. Holder leans into it and drives it through mid off for a run.
Tosses it up on off, Holder defends it off the front foot.
The edges are giving Holder a lot of runs today! Raza bowls a straighter one outside off, he tries to defend but gets an outside edge through short third man for a brace.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Length outside off, Shane guides it to gully.
Short again on off, bounces a touch more. Dowrich hops and defends it onto the ground. He does well to keep it down, it could have easily popped up in the air.
Shorter in length outside off, Dowrich guides it to point. That made a good sound off the bat.
Length again outside off, Shane defends it towards covers.
Dowrich has broken his bat as he tried to play the last delivery. He wants a replacement.
Good length on off, bounces a touch more. Hits Dowrich high on his bat as he tries to defend it.
Fuller in length on middle, Dowrich pushes it to mid on.
FOUR! Into the 90s! Raza bowls it very full outside off, Holder tries to drive but gets an outside edge through short third man for a boundary.

Good work, Chakabva! He has had a tough time with the gloves but he did well there. Raza darts it outside off, goes on with the arm and also stays low. Holder gets beaten as he tries to defend and Chakabva crouches down low and to collect it. That should give him some confidence.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fuller outside off, Dowrich pushes it towards cover for a run.
Fires it outside off, Holder taps it towards point for a quick single.
Flatter on off, Holder defends it off the front foot.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
A surprise short delivery on middle, gets big on the batsman. Dowrich does well to hop defend it down onto the ground.
Good length on off, Dowrich defends it towards covers.
Length outside off, Dowrich it not interested in playing at it.

Another huge shout from Mpofu but the umpire remains put! He has really bowled well here. He angles it into the batsman. Dowrich goes for the flick but misses to get hit on the pads. Mpofu turns back and cries for the appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Hawk Eye shows the ball is just clipping leg stump.
Good length on middle, Holder tucks it towards fine leg to change strike.
Works it with the spin to the man at short leg.
Tosses it up on off, Shane defends it solidly.
Quicker on middle, turning back in. Dowrich defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! Too easy! A half-volley by Raza outside off. Dowrich leans into it and drives it through covers for a boundary.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter on off, Dowrich drives it to mid off.
Sikandar Raza is into the attack. He was brilliant with the ball yesterday. Can he repeat his heroics today?
Fuller in length on off, Holder defends it solidly. A maiden for Mpofu. Good start with the third new ball.
Good length outside off, Holder lets it be.
Back of a length on off, Holder defends it towards point for no runs.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.

PEACH! Holder is lucky to not have edged it! Mpofu goes wide of the crease and angles it into the batsman, gets it to shape away after pitching it around off. Holder tries to defend but gets beaten. Encouraging sings for Zimbabwe as there was swing on that delivery.
Fuller in length outside off, looking for some swing but there ain't any. Holder opts not to play at it.
The third new ball is due and Zimbabwe have taken it straightaway! Can the new ball bring in some wickets? Chris Mpofu to have a go with it first.
Loopy ball outside off, Holder drives it to sweeper cover for a run.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. One run added to the total.
Floats it full on off, Dowrich keeps it out.
Loopy ball on middle, Dowrich plants his front foot forward and blocks it.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Gives it air on middle, turning away. Holder eases it down to long off for a single.
Plays it with the spin to mid off to end the over.
Fuller in length outside off, Holder drives it through covers for a run.
Floats it up on middle, Holder lunges forward in defense.
Quicker outside off, Holder looks to push it through the off side but gets beaten.

Flatter outside off, turning away. Holder tries to force it through the off side but gets an outside edge through short third man. The fielder there gives it a chase, dives and keeps it down to two. Good effort by him.
Drags his length back on leg stump, Holder flicks it to short fine leg.
Does well to block the ball on middle off the front foot.
Flighted ball on middle, turning away. Dowrich plants his front foot ahead and defends it.
A googly on middle, turning back in. Dowrich tries to defend but gets it off the inner half through short fine leg for a couple.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Loopy ball on middle, Dowrich lunges forward and defends it.
Floats it up on off, Dowrich defends it solidly.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Fuller in length outside off, Holder drives it through covers for a couple.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Tosses it up on off, Holder defends it off the front foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Drives it through mid off for a run.

DROPPED! Chakabva puts another one down! He has had a poor time with the gloves. He had this one in the gloves but then it pops out! Another reprieve for Holder. Cremer tosses it wide outside off, gets it to turn away. Holder goes for the cut but gets an outside edge to the keeper. He sticks a hand out but can't hold onto it. Had he let it go it would have been an easy catch for the slip fielder. Cremer can't believe it, as he walks back angrily towards the umpire.
Again a similar length ball, Holder again goes for the cut but is beaten by the extra bounce.
Short and wide outside off, Holder goes for the cut but is beaten.
Shorter in length outside off, Dowrich punches it through covers for a run.
Tosses it up on middle, Dowrich tries to defend but gets it off the inner half to square leg.
Loopy ball on leg stump, Dowrich drives it down to mid on.
Fuller in length this time, gets it to tail back in a touch. Jason lunges forward and blocks it.
Once again bowls it on the length around the off stump channel. Holder camps back and defends it.
Fuller in length on middle, Holder times it to mid on. That was well evaded by Dowrich as it was hit straight at him.
Slower full ball on off, Holder reads it well and defends it off the front foot.
Good length on off, Holder defends it solidly.

FOUR! Edgy! Holder almost chopped it on there. Signs of the surface getting slower. Shorter in length by Mpofu outside off, Holder goes for the cut but gets an inside edge past the off stump and down to the fine leg fence.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Slower through the air outside off, Dowrich lets the ball do its part and then guides it to point.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Tosses it up outside leg stump, turns in. Dowrich tries to defend but is struck high on the pads. The keeper makes an ambitious appeal but the umpire shakes his head. The bowler was not interested as the ball pitched outside leg.
Flatter outside off, Dowrich lets it be.
Fuller in length outside off, Holder drives it through covers for a run.

A huge appeal but nothing from the umpire. Mpofu comes running in and lands it on a length outside off, gets some sharp inward movement after pitching. Dowrich tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball also falls just short of the keeper who takes it on the bounce. Close call!
Lands it on a length again, the ball comes slowly off the surface. Dowrich defends it solidly.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Length ball on middle, Dowrich flicks it to mid-wicket.

Highest 8th wicket partnership for West Indies in Tests! Fuller in length outside off, inviting the batsman to drive. Dowrich obliges and hits it through backward point, does not quite get it off the middle but enough to collect two. 150-run stand between the two also comes up.
Good length outside off, the batsman need not play at it.
Drags his length back outside off, Dowrich cuts it through point for a run.
Quicker but shorter in length on middle, Holder rocks back and whips it against the spin through mid-wicket for a run.
Floats it full and outside off, Holder drives it to covers.
Shorter in length and turning away. Jason cuts it to the man at covers.
Flatter outside off, Holder pushes it towards mid off for no runs.
Starts off with a nice loopy ball on middle, turns away. Holder prods forward in defense.
Graeme Cremer will bowl from the other end.
Holder too gets going! Fullish length on middle, Holder tucks it around the corner to retain strike. The lead is now 50.
First run of the day! Mpofu bowls it full on middle, Dowrich flicks it through square leg for a run.
Good length on off, Dowrich defends it off the front foot.

The move to have two men at short mid-wicket almost paid off! Mpofu lands it on a length around off, gets it to jag back into the batsman. The ball also stops a little. Dowrich is early into the flick and does it uppishly but on the bounce to the man there.
Goes wide of the crease and angles it into the batsman. Dowrich defends it towards mid-wicket.
He starts off with a length delivery around off, no movement off the surface for him. Dowrich defends it off the back foot with authority.

We are ready to get underway. The men who matter are out in the middle. Jason Holder and Shane Dowrich will resume their innings. Chris Mpofu will start the proceedings for Zimbabwe. He has a gully and two short mid-wickets in place.

PITCH REPORT - Ed Rainsford says, it is sunny and the sun will beat down on the surface, causing more abrasion. Reckons there are a lot of cracks on the track. Opines the finger spinners are going to cause more problems than the wrist spinners. Ends by saying that it is an excellent Test wicket.

Hello and welcome to the 4th day of the second Test between Zimbabwe and West Indies in Bulawayo. We witnessed a day full of twists and turns yesterday. The home side had the away side on the mat but could not capitalize and it has let the advantage slip towards the tourists. Now, with two set batsmen Holder and Dowrich out there, the Windies will look to stretch their lead over the 100-run mark. However, the hosts will want to come out and wrap things up as quickly as possible if they are to get back in the game. Today promises to be an action-packed day of cricket. Stay tuned.
...Day 4, Session 1...

The hosts were made to toil hard under the sun. They bowled over 100 overs in the day, had their moments but just couldn't capitalize at the right time. The game is slowly drifting away from them and Cremer and Co. will have to regroup quickly if they are to avoid another defeat. Still, if they manage to pick the remaining wickets quickly and then bat well, you never know... this game might open up again. First session on day 4 will be crucial and could decide which way the game is heading towards. There's again an early start at 0930 local (0730 GMT). Do join us to catch all the action. Till then, it's goodbye from us. Cheers!

As it is said, Test match is all about patience. The one who shows it for a longer period of time, often holds the aces. That's exactly proved to be the case with the Windies. Holder and Dowrich didn't give up and staged a remarkable fightback. They not only wiped off the deficit but also have taken a 48-run lead which could very well prove to be a handy one. They are amidst an unbeaten 144-run stand and are not done yet. Both are approaching their respective tons and would look to build on the lead when they come out fresh tomorrow morning.

A gripping day of Test cricket comes to an end. Jason Holder and Shane Dowrich walk back with their heads held high. The duo has done a stupendous job and literally kept the hosts at bay. They were staring down the barrel at 230/7 when Sikandar Raza scalped a few quick wickets, thereby claiming his maiden Test 5-fer to gain the upper hand in this contest.
Solomon Mire angles it in on middle, Holder hangs back and defends it out towards short mid-wicket. Well done, skipper. That's STUMPS ON DAY 3, WINDIES LEAD BY 48!
A bit short and outside off, Holder punches it towards the man at short extra cover.
Mire angles it in from around off, Jason blocks it out.
On a good length and outside off, tapped towards point.
One can understand the issues Cremer is facing with the current situation. Had Mire been able to bowl much earlier, things would have eased off a bit for him and other spinners as well.

Highest Test score for Shane Dowrich! It has been a valuable knock and given that it has come when his side was in crisis will make it even more special. Sprayed on the pads, Shane clips it down to fine leg for a single.

No ball! And it's a big, big no ball. My colleague jokes saying he has given competition to Shannon Gabriel as he has overstepped by a big margin. On the pads, flicked through square leg for a single.
Fuller in length and angling in, Holder clips it to mid-wicket.
Okay then! Graeme Cremer has called Solomon Mire into the attack. He didn't bowl the entire day and now is asked to when the day is about to end. Can he bring a wicket?
Touch fuller outside off, Dowrich drives it off the front foot towards Cremer at short cover who fumbles but they don't run.
Fuller and targeting the base of middle stump, Dowrich clips it with the angle towards short mid-wicket.
Fuller and sprayed wider on off, Dowrich looks to go after it but then at the last moment leaves it alone.
A bit short and angling in, defended off the back foot towards mid on.
Length delivery, bowled a bit wider outside off, Dowrich looks to go after it but fails to get any wood on it.
Angles it in from around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Beaten! Raza drifts one across Holder and lures the West Indian skipper to go after it. He does so but it turns away to beat the outside edge. So close that was!
Shorter on middle and leg, Dowrich flicks it to deep backward square leg for a single.
Fuller around leg, defended into the ground by Shane.
Sloppy from the fielder, it's Tendai Chisoro who lets one go. Flatter delivery outside leg, clipped towards square leg where Chisoro misfields. Tired bodies? Anyway, the batsmen will run.
Once again leans forward and blocks it out on the ground.
Raza continues from around the wicket and loops it up around middle and leg. Holder prods forward in defense.

So we are done with the scheduled overs for the day. We still have 15 minutes to go and it means we can easily get in 3-4 overs. There is a bit of delay as Holder is getting some stretching from the physio while the Zimbabwe fielders enjoy some refreshments...
Fuller length delivery on off, defended by getting right behind the line of it.
Fuller in length and angling in, Dowrich presents a straight face of the bat down the ground. Good running between the wickets allows them to come back for the second.
Straighter in line of the stumps, Dowrich drives it with a straight bat down the ground.
Length delivery outside off, Shane lets it go.
Fuller in length, swinging in, played off the front foot.

A stifled appeal for an LBW! But umpire Dharmasena shakes his head! Masakadza gets one to swing back in, Dowrich tries clipping it but misses and is hit on the pads. The keeper and the bowler appeal but it was clearly going down leg. This is what Masakadza needs to bowl. Keep pitching it up.
Quicker one but around leg, Holder clips it towards short fine leg. Wants the single but Dowrich doesn't respond.
Flatter delivery around middle, defended off the back foot.
This time he is successful. Stays back and flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
A bit short and turning in from around middle, Shane tries tucking it away but misses and is hit on the pads.
Loopy delivery around middle and leg, Dowrich gets back and blocks.
Floats it up wider outside off, milked down to long off for a single.
Once again keeps it full, angles it in on middle, wristed straight towards short mid-wicket.
On a fuller length but the line is wide outside off, Dowrich shoulders his arms to it.
Fuller and on the middle stump, nudged towards mid-wicket for nothing.
Stump-to-stump line from Masakadza. Holder punches it down to long on for a single.
Hamilton spears in a fuller ball, comes back in a touch. Holder with no foot movement tries to keep it out but gets an inside edge towards the square leg fielder.
Short of a length delivery outside off, Dowrich punches it through covers for a single.
Quicker one around middle, punched off the back foot towards the bowler.
A bit of flight around middle, bunted back to the bowler.
The tall man lunges forward and dead-bats it solidly.
Goes around the wicket and bowls it around leg, Holder looks to flick but the ball turns down further and the batsman misses his attempted flick shot.
Fuller on the stumps, Shane drives it back to the bowler who fails to stop it with a dive to his right. The ball goes down to long on for a single
Flighted delivery around middle, Holder gets back and tucks it with the spin through square leg for a single.

Good take from Chakabva, this! Sprays it down leg, Dowrich misses his clip but Regis quickly moves to his left and collects it. He had a tough time with the gloves today but this should give him some confidence.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Shane waits for it and at the last moment dabs it deftly behind point for a couple of runs.
On a fuller length with no pace on it, eased through covers for a single.
Length delivery outside off, Dowrich slaps it square of the wicket on the off side for a single.
Good length delivery bowled outside off, Holder gets on top of the bounce and punches it through covers for a single.
Masakadza from over the wicket bowls a short ball outside off, Holder punches it towards the cover fielder.
Zimbabwe are wasting time now! They are doing everything slowly. They now bring Hamilton Masakadza into the attack.
Raza keeps it full on the stumps, Dowrich clips it towards silly mid on.
Floated delivery outside off, Dowrich leans forward and blocks it out.
Gets across a bit and clips it to short fine leg.
FOUR! That had to be put away and Dowrich does so! Short delivery around middle and off, Shane camps back and cuts it through covers for a boundary.
Flatter through the air around middle, Dowrich shows a straight bat.
Tossed up around middle, Dowrich defends it off the front foot.
We have a slight halt in play. Regis Chakabva seems to have sprained his ankle a bit, so is having the magic spray applied on it. The players have decided to use this break to get some refreshments.
Darts it way outside off, Holder has no intention of playing at that. Lets it be.
Slower through the air, quite loopy outside off, driven through the covers. No run taken.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
Brings the wrists into play and works it away on the leg side.
Shane Dowrich gets right behind the line of this one and blocks it out.
Quicker in pace and very close to off, spinning away a touch, Dowrich goes back and blocks.
On a bit of a fuller length, close to off, met with the full face of the bat to keep it out.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Flat, short and on the stumps, worked away in front of square leg to rotate strike.
Looped up on the stumps, Dowrich keeps bat and pad close together and blocks it out.
Straighter in line on middle and leg, defended away on the leg side, past the short leg fielder.
Down the leg side, Dowrich swivels and then helps it towards short fine leg.
Short ball around off, drags the pull through mid-wicket for one. The 350 is up for West Indies.

Ed Rainsford on air makes a real good point. He says Zimbabwe wasted a review against Powell earlier during the first session and to be honest it was really a poor call from Cremer. And then one against Holder (which was dead plumb) they couldn't opt for as they didn't have any in the bank. At that time when Holder was struck on the pads, his team was trailing by 99 runs. So it means how important it is to keep the reviews. It can completely change the course of the game, especially as according to the new rules, the reviews won't be refreshed after 80 overs...
Dropped a bit short on off, turning away, cut away hard through cover-point and the batsman crosses over.
Loopy delivery outside off, Holder drives it through the cover region for couple of runs.
Pushes it quicker through the air on off, Holder plants his front foot forward and meets it with a straight blade.
Full and outside off, drilled through towards sweeper cover for a single.
Extremely full on middle stump, jammed back to the bowler.

Drinks break! So, just 9 overs to go in the day and we have around an hour to play. It means Zimbabwe should definitely bowl more than 98 overs in the day but over rate won't be of any use. They need wickets and that too quickly as the match is slowly getting dragged away from them. If the current pair of Holder and Dowrich bats the whole day and take the lead to say over 50-odd, it could well prove to be a handy one. Final hour then, what do we have in store?
Beaten! Fuller and quicker through the air, Holder leans across to drive but there is a bit of drift and as a result Holder nearly gets an outside edge.
Goes back and clips it on the bounce towards the short leg fielder.
Tossed up ball around off, pushed into the cover region.
SIX! Down the track and bludgeons it, does Holder! He gets to the pitch of the delivery this time and unfurls a clean strike over long on for a maximum.

Uppish but no damage done! Raza floats it up around middle and leg, Holder clears the front leg to hit it across the line but seems to have been deceived in the flight. Drags it off the inner half towards wide long on for a couple.
Flighted delivery outside off, Jason drives it towards mid off by making a bit of room.
This one dips in around the pads, flicked to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Jason Holder leans forward, keeps his bat close to the pad and smothers it out.
Loopy delivery down leg, Dowrich gets down and sweeps it to deep backward square leg for a single.
Around leg, tucked towards mid-wicket.
Gives it loop and bowls it full outside off, Holder makes room and drives it down to long off for a single.
Loopy delivery outside leg, Holder takes a stride forward and smothers it down.
Dowrich leans forward and dead-bats it.
Tossed up outside off, driven towards cover.
Fuller on the stumps, driven back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Around middle and leg, pushed towards mid on.
Gets forward and defends it down.

FOUR! Reverse sweeps and connects one this time! It's also a moment for the skipper to rejoice, it's his 7th Test fifty! Raises the bat to the dressing room and they all laud the effort! Loopy ball outside leg, Holder gets down and nails the reverse sweep behind point for a boundary.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Brings up the 100-run stand now! What a turnaround from these two this! They are going from strength to strength. Fuller ball on middle, driven down to long on for a single.
Flatter delivery outside off, Dowrich rocks back to pull but the ball sneaks under his bat and goes between his legs to the keeper.

There you go! This could be risky Mr. Dowrich! When you are trying to pad it away if it's pitched outside leg then you need to keep your front leg in line. He fails to do so as the ball spins in and hits the back leg and nearly rolls on to the stumps.
Cremer bowls it down leg, Dowrich lets it be.
Short delivery on middle, pulled through mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted delivery on the stumps, blokced into the ground.
Darted on the pads, whipped to deep mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter again, defended off the back foot comfortably.
Flatter on middle, clipped on the bounce to short leg.
As expected, Cremer wants a wicket and he goes to his star man. Sikandar Raza is brought back into the attack. Can this man provide a breakthrough again?
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

On middle and leg, clipped towards short fine leg for a single. West Indies are now officially into the lead. This has been a superb effort from these two. At one stage it seemed like they won't even wipe the deficit out. Can they swell it to somewhere near 100? If they do, they will have a great chance to seal this one.
Goes deep in the crease and tucks it around the corner.
Pitches it outside leg, Jason Holder leans ahead to defend but it goes off the outer half of the bat towards the off side.
Gets down to play the reverse sweep now but is beaten again.
That ball nearly rolls back on the stumps! Spinning in from outside off, Holder looks to drive but gets an inside edge which nearly rolls back on the stumps.

The commentators on air discuss as to what should Cremer do now? The bowlers look down and out. His spinners are being dealt with ease at the moment. Should he risk bringing an injured Solomon Mire back on? Because Tendai Chisoro has already bowled over 35 overs and looks tired. Let's see what does Cremer opt for.
SCORES ARE LEVEL NOW! Chisoro drops it a bit short outside off, Jason Holder punches it through the same region and settles for one.
West Indies just trail by 1 run! Short and outside off, cracked off the back foot towards cover for a couple.
Holder takes a stride forward and blocks it into the ground.
Leans forward and buries it into the ground.
A bit too full, served outside off, driven towards backward point.
Flighted delivery outside off, turning away, Holder makes an easy leave.
On the flatter trajectory, turning in, Dowrich has his stumps covered and shows a straight bat.
A bit too full on middle, bunted back to the bowler.
Shane has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tries to put bat on ball to the delivery pitched on leg, misses and is hit on the pads.
From around the wicket, Cremer bowls it outside leg, Dowrich pads it away.
Floated ball on the stumps, driven towards long off for a single.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Takes a long stride forward does Holder and drives it towards cover.
Goes back and pushes it with the turn towards point.
Flighted delivery outside off, Holder looks to drive it away but is beaten by the away turn.
Flatter on off, left alone.
Shortish ball outside off, Holder cuts it towards extra cover.
Loopy full toss on middle and leg, flicked to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Holder takes a stride forward and stonewalls it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Goes around the wicket now, lands it around the rough, Holder defends.
Cremer once again bowls a short ball, luckily for him Dowrich finds the man in the deep at mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter through the air around middle, punched off the back foot towards mid-wicket.
Short and outside off, punched towards sweeper cover for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Darted on middle, blocked.

FOUR! There it is! 6th Test fifty for Shane Dowrich! It means so much to him, he punches the air in joy. Skipper Holder acknowledges it as well. He needed this as he was having a lean patch with the bat since a while. Very full outside off, Dowrich opens the bat face and gets it through backward point for a boundary.
Fires it full on middle, blocked by getting behind the line.

Almost... that just bounced over the stumps! A bit slower through the air, Dowrich rocks back to punch it through the line but gets a bottom edge which just goes over the stumps to the keeper. No luck for the hosts whatsoever.
Flatter delivery outside off, Dowrich dabs it square of the wicket on the off side. The fielder gives it a chase but they run three.

FOUR! That had HIT ME written all over it! This is really poor bowling from Cremer. Once again drags his length short, easy pickings for Dowrich who rocks back and pummels it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Flighted leg break outside off, pushed with an angled bat towards point.
A bit too full on middle, driven back to the bowler.
Cremer drops it short, turning away, this time Holder hits it through backward point for a single.
Turning away from a length, Holder cuts it to point.
Graeme Cremer to bowl now.
Slider around middle, kept out off the front foot.
Lets the ball turn and then dabs it towards backward point.
Flatter outside off, left alone.
FOUR! What a shot, that! Chisoro gives nice flight but drops it in Dowrich's arc who smashes it straight back over the bowler's head for a boundary.
Flighted delivery outside off, thrashed towards sweeper cover for a single.
Beaten! Chisoro lands it on a length around off, Holder leans across to defend but the ball turns away and beats the outside edge of Holder's bat. Tendai needs some fortunes here.
Once again a slower delivery on the stumps, Dowrich defends.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short and wider on off, Jason Holder quickly opts to pull seeing the length. But ends up dragging it through mid-wicket for a single.
Mpofu once again bowls a slower fuller ball on off, Holder doesn't get greedy seeing it. He just pushes it towards the mid on fielder.
Short of a length delivery on middle, Jason gets right behind the line and offers a straight bat.
Mpofu rolls his fingers over the ball, bowls it on middle, Holder works it straight to mid on.
Flatter and quicker through the air outside off, Dowrich lets it be.
Fuller in length and angling in, blocked off the front foot.
Flatter delivery outside off, Holder rocks back and thrashes it through covers for a single.
Flighted delivery outside off, driven hard but finds the man at extra cover.
Flighted delivery on middle, nudged through mid-wicket for a single.
Too full around off, driven towards the man at mid off.
FOUR! Runs continue to leak! Short of a length delivery on the body, Holder swivels and pulls it with complete control through backward square leg. Second boundary of the over, 10 off it!
On a fuller length on off, pushy drive but straight to the cover fielder.
FOUR! Up and over! This is good batting from the skipper. He sees the length, picks it up early and smokes it over mid off. Hits it cleanly and picks up a boundary to his name.

A loud shout for an LBW! Chris angles it in on a fuller length, it keeps nipping back in, Holder tries to slog it across the line but misses and is hit on the pads. The Zimbabwe players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Replays show why, there was a faint inside edge.
Silly mid on in place.
Back of a length delivery on middle, Holder defends it down.
Mpofu angles it in from over the wicket, Holder lunges forward to defend but there is a little bit of inward movement and hence it goes off the inner half through backward square leg for a couple.
Chris Mpofu is asked to bowl from the other end.
Fires a low full toss on middle, driven easily down to mid on.
Short and turning away after pitching, punched off the back foot towards point.
Full and delivered around off, defended into the ground.
Floated ball outside off, driven straight to the cover fielder.
A bit of flight outside off, pushed off the front foot towards cover.
Chisoro from around the wicket loops it up around off, Dowrich presses forward in defense.
The players return for play. The two West Indian batsmen are Jason Holder and Shane Dowrich. Zimbabwe begin the session with Tendai Chisoro taking the ball first up....
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

The Zimbabwe spinners would need to be patient to induce false strokes. They looked flat in the second hour and bowled too many short balls. Can they pick the remaining three wickets quickly or will the current pair bat well to wipe off the deficit and take a handy lead? Join us in a short while to see what happens next...

Session highlights - 32 Overs, 100 Runs, 3 Wickets! A fairly good session for both the sides. The hosts had a good first hour where they got timely breakthroughs, courtesy Sikandar Raza who registered his maiden 5-fer and spun the web magnificently to dictate terms. Just when it seemed like Zimbabwe would run through the batting line-up, Holder and Dowrich denied them. The duo took their time to get in and once they did, they got some freebies which indeed helped their cause. The current stand is worth 58 but the important thing from West Indies' point of view is that they are trailing by just 38 runs now.
Flighted ball around middle and leg, Shane Dowrich lunges forward and wrists it through mid-wicket for one. TEA ON DAY 3!
Googly on middle, tucked towards backward square leg.
Tosses it up around middle and leg, milked down to long on for a single.
Short and turning away once again, Holder tries cutting it away but mistimes it towards short cover.
Flighted delivery on middle, defended by coming forward.
A bit short on off, Jason Holder cuts it with the spin towards point.
Graeme Cremer to bowl the last over before tea. Can he strike?
Flat ball around middle and off, SD rocks back to keep it out.
Gets nicely forward and blocks it into the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Zimbabwe spinners are bowling too many short balls! Drops it short on middle, Dowrich camps back and pulls it over mid-wicket and gets two for doing so.
Floated ball outside off, defended towards the short cover fielder.
Loops it up on off, Holder takes his front foot across and eases it down to long off for a single.
A bit too full on middle, Shane leans ahead and blocks.
Tossed up delivery on middle, swept towards backward square leg.
Fuller on off, driven past the diving extra cover fielder for a single.

Slides it across and stays a bit low as well, Dowrich goes deep in the crease and does extremely well to cut it through backward point. He calls for the third and gets it comfortably in the end. Good running! 50-run stand comes up as well!
Flattish through the air, blocked off the back foot.
Raza comes from around the wicket and pitches it on middle, punched towards mid on.
Flighted delivery around middle and off, Holder prods forward in defense.
Holder comes forward again to defend but the ball turns away, takes the outside edge of the bat and rolls towards point.
A bit flatter through the air around middle, Holder uses the depth of the crease and whips it through mid-wicket to collect two.
Drops it around middle, turns towards off, Holder leans forward to defend.
Fires it on middle, Jason gets low and jams it out back to the bowler.
Tossed up on off, driven towards cover.
Tendai Chisoro is brought back into the attack.
Blocked off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! The deficit is brought under 50 now! This is good batting from the duo! Loopy ball outside off, Dowrich presses forward and strokes it beautifully through covers for a boundary.
Gets back quickly to this short ball and offers a straight bat.
Loops it up outside off, Dowrich lunges forward in defense.
Loopy delivery on off, blocked watchfully off the front foot.
Gets back and works it with the spin towards mid-wicket.
FOUR! Runs coming thick and fast for the Windies! Cremer floats it up wider outside off, Holder takes the aerial route and lofts it inside out over extra cover for a boundary.
Tossed up on off, pushed towards mid off.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Cremer serves a gift to his opposite number. He drops it short on middle, Holder is quick to pounce on it. He rocks back and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Takes a long stride forward and smothers it down.
Flattish through the air around middle, Holder gets back and defends.
Floats it up around middle and leg, the batsman gets forward and nudges it away.
Fired on leg, worked towards backward square leg.
FOUR! Beautiful shot! Raza gives it a decent flight, bowls it near middle and off, Dowrich comes down the track and drives it cleanly through mid off to pick up the second boundary of the over.
Lands it around leg, Dowrich goes back to flick but gets it off the pads towards short leg.
FOUR! Put away! Raza drops it short on middle, Dowrich rocks back and pulls it hard. The man at short leg takes the evasive action and the ball travels uppishly through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Tosses up on leg, Dowrich looks to flick but fails to get any wood on it. Chakabva behind the stumps juggles and collects it somehow. He appeals but nothing from the umpire.
The seam is coming off from the ball. Umpire Dharmasena removes the scissor and does the needful.
Flighted delivery on middle, bunted back to the bowler.
Goes back to this flatter one and keeps it out gently.

Shout for a catch at short leg! A bit slower through the air, dipping in, Holder tries to go for the big slog across the line but misses and it lobs off something towards short leg. They appeal but nothing from the umpire. Replays show it went off the pads.
Loopy ball around off, Jason prods forward in defense.
Flatter delivery around middle, Holder hangs back and defends.
Tossed up delivery around middle, Holder takes a stride forward and defends.
Tossed up delivery on the off stick, Dowrich comes ahead and smothers the ball in its tracks. Windies still trail by 69 runs.
Takes the aerial route and clears the infield with ease. Holder slog sweeps it over mid-wicket and crosses over.
Straighter in line and going on straight, on the stumps, blocked.
Picks it off his pads and tucks it away through backward square leg for a run.
Full and straight on the stumps, drilled back down to the bowler again.
Continues from around the wicket and tosses it up on off, drilled back down the track towards the bowler.
The googly on middle and leg, Holder doesn't exactly pick it up. Gets a leading which makes its way towards mid-wicket.
Hangs deep inside his crease and blocks it out with a straight blade.
Touch short again outside off, patted away to the covers from the back foot for a single.
Shane Dowrich has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fuller in length again, kept out off the front foot.
FOUR! Cremer has a tendency of doing that, he does occasionally drop it short. Dowrich latches onto it and cuts it square through point for a boundary.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.

Flatter, quicker and down the leg side, Holder looks to swing it away square on the leg side but misses. Raza however doesn't think so. As Chakabva is unable to gather it cleanly, he goes down in disappointment.
Loopy and fullish in length again, Holder prods forward to block it out.
Makes use of his feet, gets to the pitch of the ball and hits the ball off the inside edge on the leg side.
Floats it up on middle and off, Holder comes ahead and blocks.

Oh dear, oh dear! Umpire Dharmasena has got that completely wrong. Jason Holder survives but he should have been out of here. Sikandar Raza denied another wicket. Comes from around the wicket and bowls an off spinner on off, Holder is back to defend but is caught on the pads. Loud appeal, nothing from the umpire. He indicates there's an inside edge but replays confirm there's no bat involved. The Windies skipper gets a life.

FOUR! Good shot, it's earned him a much-needed boundary. Too straight in line on a fuller length, Dowrich flicks it elegantly through the mid-wicket region. The man in the deep runs fast to his left in an attempt to stop it but it's too far away from him. The 250 is up for Windies now.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fuller in length on the stumps, wristed down the ground to long on for a single.
Looped up outside off, Holder is a bit early into the drive. Chips it in front of Brendan Taylor at cover-point who dives to his left and stops it.

Should have been forward but Holder is caught in his crease. Could have been his undoing. Just back of a driving length, Holder is two minds about what to do, just loosely plays at it away from his body and the spinning ball beats the outside edge of his bat.
Overpitched on off, allows Holder to push the ball away to the covers before it turns.
Jason Holder comfortably punches this down to long on for a single. Wasn't much turn on it, which made it easier for him to play the shot.
Shorter and flat on middle and off, whipped away through the mid-wicket region to get off strike.
Darts it on off stump, Shane meets the ball by bringing down a straight blade.
At 82 kph, Raza attacks the stumps. The batsman is well forward in defense.
Quicker in pace again, punched back to the bowler this time off the back foot.
Pushes it quicker through the air with minimal air around off, Dowrich gets back and punches it out.
Full around leg, wristed just wide of mid on for an easy run.
Short and wide outside off, turning away, Dowrich should have put this away but can only find the man at point.
Moves inside his crease well. Stays right behind the line and presents a tight defensive shot to keep it out.
Not much turn here, allows Shane to turn it away towards backward square leg.
Ripper from Cremer! Lands it on middle and off and it just takes off. Spins a lot as well and beats the outside edge of Shane Dowrich's bat.
A lot of air from the leggie, but it's too full on middle, Dowrich forces it to mid off by clearing his front leg.
Knocks this full delivery down to mid on by leaning ahead.
FOUR! Beautiful shot. Full outside off, Holder uses his reach well and drives it through the line. The fielder attempts to chase it down but cannot stop it before it reaches the cover boundary.
An appreciable amount of turn for Sikandar, Jason Holder goes with the turn and bisects the gap between mid-wicket and mid on for a double.
Spinning in, it's played with soft hands in front of short leg.
Some flight on this from Raza, attacks the stumps as Holder takes a big lunge forward to defend.
Quicker delivery on the off stick, Holder is careful as he blocks it out back down the track.
Darted fuller outside off, no shot offered by the batsman.
Full in length once again, stroked through the covers for one.

Nicely done! Tossed up outside off, Dowrich leans into the stroke before the ball can turn and drives it through the gap in the covers. Solomon Mire chases after it and just about manages to pull it back inside the rope. Saves a vital run for his side.
Floated delivery from Gremer, Dowrich with a solid front foot defense.
Tad short again and outside off, Dowrich taps it away on the off side.
Turning away from the Windies skipper from around off, Jason Holder off the back foot punches it down to long off for a single.
Graeme Cremer comes back on.
Goes with the turn again and punches it straight to Graeme Cremer at short mid-wicket.
Positions himself perfectly behind the line and defends.
Quite full again from Raza, another front foot defensive shot by the batsman.
Turning in a long way on leg, Dowrich moves inside his crease and whips it past short leg.
Loopy and full on middle and leg, Holder comes forward and wrists it down to long on for a single.
Jason Holder, the Windies skipper, is the new man in. He has a big job in front of him. His team needs him to really step up.

Drinks break! What an incredible phase of play for the hosts. Sikandar Raza has done all the damage with his three wickets and dismissed the Windies' middle order in no time at all. Matter of cleaning up the tail now for Zimbabwe, can they do it quickly?

OUT! Sikandara Raza, oh you masterful beauty! 3 wickets in no time and it's the dangerman Shai Hope who's been sent back. Windies in the deep end here now, brilliant from the offie. He changes the angle and comes from around the wicket, flights in on middle. Hope is forward and plays for the turn when there is none. Proves to be his undoing as the ball goes straight on. Takes the off stump with it and that spells the end to Shai Hope's innings. Maiden 5-fer for Sikandar Raza, he's been superb since he's come on to bowl.
This time Dowrich unfurls the cut and places it behind square on the leg side. Third man inside the ring chases after it and keeps the batsmen down to two.
Short and wide outside off, Hope cuts it from the back foot through point and gets a run for doing so.
Leans across and knocks this full ball into the covers.
Darts it full and outside off, left alone.
Not much turn on this occasion, Shai Hope reads the line well and blocks.
Shai Hope hangs back to this shorter ball and punches it to covers.
Flicked to the mid-wicket fielder again and it's the end of the over.
Shortens the length a bit on this occasion, Dowrich is on the back foot as he defends it with a straight blade.
Pushes it to the cover region. Another dot ball.
Another one played with the spin. Flicked to mid-wicket for nothing.
Straighter one on the stumps, played back to the bowler.
Dowrich watches this very close as he turns it towards the mid-wicket area. Stays inside the crease and plays it well.
Comes forward, gets to the pitch of the ball and meets it at its pitch.
Flat and short, Hope from within the crease blocks it out.
Some flight again and outside off, Dowrich gets an outside edge which runs down towards third man for a single.
Looped up on middle and off, blocked off the front foot with the full face of the bat.
Spinning away from around off, played away towards point for a single.
Flatter around off, kept out by getting behind the line.
Shane Dowrich is the next man in.

OUT! It's Sikandar Raza again, Zimbabwe's He-Man! What a player. Comes in and got two wickets in quick succession. Brings his side right back into this contest. Spinning in around off, Blackwood goes back and works it uppishly on the leg side. Straight into the hands of Graeme Cremer at short mid-wicket who takes a good catch. Throws it in the air and celebrates loudly, he knows this is their opening to get in. Blackwood departs, Windies in some trouble. These are now Raza's best figures in Test match cricket.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floats it up around off, another front foot defense by the batsman.
Drags the length back around off, kept out off the back foot.
Provides some decent air around off, Jermaine plants his front foot forward and meets it with the full face of the bat.
Some turn and bounce for Raza. Kicks off the deck a bit and goes off the inside edge of Blackwood's bat and flies past short leg.
Off the back foot again, bit quicker and flatter on off, turned towards mid-wicket for a single.
Jermaine Blackwood has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Brings the wrists into the play and works it on the leg side.
Some extra loop from the left-armer, Blackwood is forward in defense.
Against the spin this time, some bite on this for Chisoro. He goes back and works it away on the leg side for one.
Straighter on the stumps, Hope stays right behind the line and defends.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Zimbabwe excited, half-celebrate but then that's short lived. Spinning in sharply on middle and leg, Blackwood goes back to tuck it away and it lobs off his pads to short leg. They thought there was bat, but that wasn't the case.
FOUR! Turning in on middle and leg, Blackwood is off the mark in a flash! Rocks back and pulls it through backward square leg for a boundary.
Jermaine Blackwood is the next batsman in.

OUT! HE'S GONE! This is a big wicket and it's Sikandar Raza again who's got the breakthrough! Zimbabwe needed the wicket and he's done it for his side. Chase played his part too, bit of an unnecessary shot to play with the ball turning so much. Landed around off and it spins in a touch, Chase brings out the reverse sweep and does not connect. Is caught on the front pad and after a long hard think, umpire Dharmasena raises his finger in response to the appeal. Roston reviews it almost immediately and replays show the impact is umpire's call and the ball is clipping the leg stump, which is also the umpire's call. So, he has to go back. The review isn't wasted but the decision stays. The 56-run stand has been broken.
Review time! Roston Chase has been caught leg before and adjudged out. He's quickly taken the review. Looks like he might be gone...
Once again he works it away on the leg side. No run taken.
Off spinner outside off, Chase plays with the turn and works it on the leg side.
Sikandar Raza returns.
Outside off, placed to point for no run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Loud shout for an lbw! It's close, really close, but the umpire doesn't think so. On off again and it spins away a shade, Hope is back again in defense and is caught on the pads. Big, big appeal from the Windies, but since the impact is outside off, however marginal it may be, the umpire declines.

Dropped! There was a clear edge, oh boy! Regis Chakabva should have taken that. Classical delivery from Tendai Chisoro. Lands it on middle and gets it to turn just enough. Hope who is back to defend is squared up a touch and gets a feather. It goes behind and the keeper cannot hold onto it. Big chance, could very well come back to haunt them.
Very full on off with some drift into Shai Hope, he strides ahead and blocks.
Spinning away on a shorter length, outside off, cracked square through point which enables Roston to take a run.
Veering back in on middle and leg, full in length, flicked through the right of the short mid-wicket to keep strike.
Fullish in length attacking the stumps, tapped in front of mid-wicket for a brisk run.
On the pads again, flicked away on the leg side for a single.

FOUR! Comfortably done. Easy for any batsman in the world really to put that away. Angling down leg, Chase just helps it along its way and across the fine leg fence for a boundary. With that, the 50-run stand is up as well.

Smartly bowled by Chris Mpofu. Takes the pace off it and bowls an off cutter around off, it comes back in and goes past the inside edge of Chase's bat who is done in because of the lack of pace. Kept a little low too.
On a good length well outside off, no way the batsman will bother himself with that.
On the fuller side of things once more, some more flight on it this time. Shai Hope meets it with the full face of the bat to end the over.
Tossed right up there, Hope presses forward and buries it into the track.
Pushes this full delivery just wide of the mid off fielder and both batsmen scurry across for a quick single. Nicely done.
Looped up outside off, driven into the off side for a single.

Almost had him! Almost. Too close for comfort for Shai Hope. He goes deep inside the crease to flick it away but the ball is pushed quicker through the air this time. Almost raps him on the pads as he just manages to get some bat on it and put it away on the leg side.
Drifting in on middle and leg, a bit too straight in line which allows Hope to works it to square leg.
Back of a length, moving into the batsman off the seam, Chase is watchful as he taps it down on the off side with soft hands.
Short of a good length into the body, he swivels inside the line and helps the pull behind square leg for a single.
Keeps it full again but keep it close to off this time, a solid drive from Hope which finds the man at mid on.

FOUR! That's an excellent shot! The sound off the bat was majestic, nicely timed. Gentle half-volley outside off, Shai Hope leans into the shot and drives it through the gap in the covers for a boundary.
Shaping back in on a fuller length, worked away to mid-wicket off the inner half.

Great effort from PJ Moor! Saved a certain boundary there. Length delivery outside off, Hope cuts this hard square of the wicket. Moor at point dives full stretch to his right, gets a hand to it and parries it towards covers. Saves two vital runs for his side.
Floats it up outside the line of off stump, pushed into the covers for a single.
Stays deep inside the crease to this flat ball and offers a firm punch to long on for a single.
Fired down the leg side, Hope makes room and looks to flick, but it goes off his pads and down the leg side as the batsmen take a leg bye.

FOUR! Poor ball and it's dispatched! He's not going to miss out on those, Shai Hope. Short and flat around off, he picks up the length early, rocks back and muscles the pull over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Oooh! Close. Chisoro darts it quick on middle and off, Hope shuffles across, gets behind the line and just about manages to bring his bat down to defend.
From around the wicket, it's dropped short outside off, Roston Chase goes back and cuts it to sweeper cover for one.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, another easy leave for the batsman.
Cutting back in from outside off, Hope covers the line well and lets it be.
Hurls in on a slightly fuller length on the fifth stump line, left alone by Shai Hope.
Similar length delivery, Roston leans into it and strokes it to covers for an easy single.
Full length delivery outside off, Chase goes for an expansive drive but mistimes it back to Chisoro.
Sits deep in the crease to the flatter delivery and works it to square leg for a run.
Quicker through the air, spinning away. Roston lets it go.
Drifting in with the arm, Chase makes room and drives it crisply to covers.
Subtle change of pace from Chisoro. It is in line of the stumps as Chase answers it with a straight bat.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! Short and room on offer, Chase makes good use of the crease and slaps it through the vacant point region for a boundary.
Tossed up on off, Chase presses forward and eases it off the front foot to covers.
Keeps it nice and full again, Shai jams it out back to the bowler.
Similar delivery, driven nicely but straight to the same fielder.
Full delivery, a bit of inward swing. Shai covers the line and eases it off the front foot to mid on.
Length delivery in the zone of apprehension, Shai Hope points his bat skywards and allows it through.
Intent from Mpofu! Full length ball attacking the stumps, Hope drives it straight back to Mpofu who picks it up and mimes a throw at the keeper's end.
Low full toss on off, Shai whips it straight to the man at short mid-wicket.
Chris Mpofu to share the attack from the other end.
Floats it up outside off, driven towards extra cover. A maiden to start with!
Slider around middle and leg, Chase misses his tuck and is hit on the pads.
Gets behind the line and keeps it out.
Floats it up outside off, driven off the outer half of the bat towards backward point.
Bowls it around off, it turns away, left alone.
From around the wicket, Tendai fires in a fuller ball on middle, it's jammed out well by Chase.

Welcome back for the second session! The Windies batsmen, Chase and Hope are back in the middle. Will they dominate the session? Let's wait and find out. Tendai Chisoro will be the one to start first up. A slip and a short leg in place.
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

With the way the track is deteriorating, it will be a stern test for the batsmen. Will the hosts dominate the afternoon session or will the pair of Hope and Chase keep them at bay? Let's find out shortly...

The spinners extracted a lot of spin and bounce and kept the batsmen on their toes. It was Raza who provided two important breakthroughs. Powell was riding his luck but finally departed after being put down thrice by Cremer, thereby missing out on a ton by a mere 10 runs.

It has been a really action-packed session of cricket - 40 overs, 110 runs, 3 wickets. The day begun with Powell and the nightwatchman, Bishoo braving out the spinners. Both of them took initiative and scored at a good click. However, once Bishoo's gritty resistance came to a close and the 55-run stand ended, the visitors once again went into their shell, allowing the opposition to take hold of things.
FOUR! Confidence at its best! Full toss in line of the stumps, Hope backs away and whacks it through extra cover to find the fence. THAT'S LUNCH ON DAY 3!
Slow through the air, driven off the inner half down the track.
Loopy ball, Chase tries to whip it across but ends up dragging it through mid-wicket. Three runs taken.
Short delivery, punched off the back foot to mid off.
Flatter delivery, blocked from the crease.
SIX! Ultra positive batting from Chase! Tossed up delivery on middle, Chase clears his front leg and tonks it down the ground to send it sailing over the fence. He hit that clean as a whistle.
There is still a minute to go and the umpires say we can get one more over in. Skipper Graeme Cremer comes on to bowl...

Seems like a movie is in its climax phase. Quicker through the air on leg stump, Hope makes room to bludgeon it over covers but gets beaten on the outside edge. Chakabva behind the stumps fails to collect it cleanly. That was close to the edge as well as to the off stump. End of an eventful over.
Should be the last ball before lunch...
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On a flatter trajectory, eased to the same region.
Hangs back to the flatter delivery and pushes it to covers.
Now that is unplayable! Lands on middle and spins away with appreciable bounce. Hope looks to counter it by staying back but has no answer to the ripper.
A lot of oohs and aahs from the home side. They are in the zone at the moment. Quicker through the air, drifting towards the leg stump. Hope keeps it out off the inner half of the bat.
Ooh.. close shave! A touch fuller around off, shaping in. Chase is a little late on it but manages to get an inside edge onto his pads.
Mpofu comes back to over the wicket and bowls it on a length in the zone of apprehension. No such movement there and Roston makes an easy leave.
Bouncer this time but the direction is not right. It is down the leg side and there is no trouble for Chase to leave it.
Mpofu switches his angle and comes around the wicket. Bowls a shortish delivery on off, Chase rises with the bounce and keeps it out safely.
Back of a length delivery outside off, shoots off the deck. Chase lifts his bat skywards to allow it through.
Good length delivery in the off stump channel, Chase hangs back and defends it stoutly.
Leg gully in place for Roston Chase.
Quicker through the air, Shai hops back and answers it with a straight bat.
Slower through the air on middle, Hope lunges forward in defense.
Slider on this occasion, Shai reads it and blocks it nicely.
The new ball needs trimming. Out comes the scissor and the necessary has been done.
Quicker delivery in line of the stumps, Hope hangs back and punches it back to Chisoro.
Slower through the air, defended solidly off the front foot.
FOUR! That's a gift and it is duly accepted! Juicy full toss outside off, Hope flat-bats it over mid off to pick up a boundary.
Short delivery on middle, Hope drags his pull to fine leg for a run.
Slower delivery on a fullish length on off, Hope looks to keep it out but the bat turns in his hands and he gets it off the inner half to mid-wicket.
Very full on middle, Shai blocks it to mid-wicket. Mpofu has his tail up.
Yorker on middle, Hope jams it out to mid on.

A lot happening at the moment! Good length delivery on middle and leg, Hope hops back and tries to tuck it through square leg but misses to get pinged on the pads. Mpofu appeals loudly along with his teammates but the umpire shakes his head. Mpofu has a look at his skipper but there is no more review left. The height was a factor there.
In the channel outside off, Hope lets it go.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
FOUR! Nicely done! Shorter in length in line of the stumps, Chase rocks back and whips it uppishly through mid-wicket to find the fence.
Flatter one, kept out watchfully.
Coming in with the arm, worked through mid-wicket for a brace.
Shorter in length, punched off the back foot to covers.

Is that another dropped catch? No, the replays confirm it isn't. On a flatter trajectory on off, Chase strides forward to defend but keeps his bat inside the line. The keeper fails to collect it cleanly. The sound was of the bat hitting the pad.
Length delivery on off, Hope hangs back and the ball hits the high part of his willow. A terrific over from Mpofu.
Angling into Chase who works it through square leg for a run.
Welcomes Chase with a sharp bouncer around off, he ducks under it quickly to evade it. Mpofu is breathing fire at the moment.
Roston Chase is the new man in. He scored a 95 in the second innings of the first Test. West Indies are in a tricky position at the moment. Can he steady the ship for them?

OUT! Brilliant, brilliant bowling from Mpofu! Finally, Powell runs out of his luck after being dropped thrice by Cremer. Mpofu steams in from around the wicket and bowls a short delivery outside off, coming in with the angle with extra bounce. Powell is taken aback and is caught in a tangle. Tries to fend it away with a hop but gets a thick outside edge towards Craig Ervine at gully. He dives full length to his right and takes a gem of a catch. The umpires check for the side no ball and then the front foot no ball but it is fine. Mpofu is absolutely pumped up. The effort ball works wonders for him. He gets his first wicket of the series. The Windies had cleaned up the opposition with the second new ball yesterday. Can the home side do the same?
Slanting away from Powell, he plants his front foot across and lets it go.
Good length delivery, Powell makes good use of the depth of the crease and answers it with a straight bat.
Shortish delivery on off, Shai is in two minds whether to leave it or play at it. He eventually pokes at it and gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Risky! Flat and quick on off, Hope somehow manages to jam it out to backward point.
Coming in with the arm, Shai looks to turn it away but is struck on the pads. It will be better if Chisoro varies his pace on this track. He is only bowling quick at the moment.
Tossed up on off, spinning away. Hope is composed in his leave.
Well bowled! Quicker through the air around off, Shai plays for the spin but there is none. An outside edge is induced past the first slip fielder. Two runs taken.
Short delivery, Hope cuts it with the spin to the man at backward point.
Tendai Chisoro to share the second new ball from the other end. A slip and short leg in place for him.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Powell doesn't fiddle with it.
Wider outside off, an easy leave for the southpaw.
Once again on a full length, allowing the ball to swing. Powell covers the line and defends it nicely.
Movement again! Fullish delivery, shaping away. Hope stands his ground and looks to block it but gets an inside edge onto his pads. His partner calls him through for a run and they steal it.
Another full delivery outside off, swinging away. Shai Hope plants his front foot across and lets it go.
Right on the money! Starts off with a very full delivery outside off, Hope tries to carve it away through square of the wicket on the off side but misses.
The second new ball is available and it has been taken straightaway. Chris Mpofu is the lone frontline seamer and he will have a burst with it.
Quicker through the air outside off, Powell waits for it and glides it down to third man for a couple.
Hangs back to the flatter delivery and defends it solidly.
Floated delivery, Powell comes forward and defends it.
On a flatter trajectory, Powell hangs back and plays it to point.
In line of the stumps, Powell strides forward and blocks it solidly.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Masakadza walks off the field. He was hit hard in the hand in the previous over and seems to be hurt. Hope he is alright.
Outside off, Powell waits for it and dabs it to third man. Three runs taken.
Slow through the air, patted back to the bowler. Cremer picks it up and throws it in frustration. It hits Masakadza straight on his hands in the first slip region and he rings it in pain.

Dropped! This is the third time Cremer has put Powell down off his own bowling. He dropped the southpaw twice on 11 and now on 85. Tossed up on middle, Powell drills it straight back to the skipper who tries to take it with both his hands but the ball pops out. This was not easy but needs to be taken at this point of the game. Powell must be thanking his stars. He is leading a charmed life.
Hope has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Tossed up delivery, Hope lunges forward in defense.
Slow through the air, eased off the front foot to the cover region.
That's a peach, past the outside edge again. Slow through the air on middle, Kieran prods forward to block it but is foxed by the massive turn and bounce.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Turn and bounce again! Tossed up on middle, Powell lunges forward to defend but the ball turns away to beat the outside edge of the bat.
Shorter in length, Powell hangs back and blocks it solidly to covers.
Makes room to the flighted delivery and stonewalls it.
Quicker in pace, defended solidly off the back foot.
Floated outside off, eased to covers.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Half-tracker on middle, Hope rocks back and pulls it with aplomb over mid-wicket to pick up a boundary. The visitors need much more of those.
Looks to keep this one out but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Fullish in length, eased to mid on for a quick run.
Floated delivery, Powell strides forward and blocks it solidly.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Hangs back to the quicker delivery and blocks it solidly.
Hangs back and tucks it to the leg side.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.

Not Out! One of the worst reviews that must have been taken. There was no bat as well. Tossed up outside off, coming in with the arm. Powell looks to keep it out but seems to have been struck on the back pad. Raza is very confident and the keeper also appeals loudly. The bowler is adamant and goes up to his skipper. Eggs him to challenge the decision and he does so. Time for the replays. They show that the ball has brushed the back pad but the impact is miles outside off, confirms the Hawk Eye. Zimbabwe exhaust both their reviews.

Howzzat? The Zimbabwe players are getting excited and there is a long discussion. It is for an LBW decision against Powell and they challenge the decision. Was there bat? Seems to be pad first but the impact is a question.
Hope is on the move as he eases it to deepish mid on for a run.
Hangs back to the flatter delivery and blocks it.

West Indies have only scored 16 from the last 11 overs that means, only one and a half per over. Till Bishoo was at the crease, they had scored 53 in 15 overs but since his dismissal, they are crawling at a snail's pace. It is not good to get in your shell.
Down the leg side, Kieran looks to work it away but is hit on the thigh pad.
Spinning into Powell who works it to backward square leg.
Floated outside off, eased off the front foot to covers.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On middle and leg, helped away towards square leg.

Short delivery, pulled away to the leg side. Not sure where the ball is as the cameraman is failing to spot it. We have the replays now. It was hit straight to Ervine at short leg who took a blow on his leg.
Hope is looking jittery, very unlike him. Floated outside off, Shai goes for a booming drive but mistimes it down the track.
Fullish around off, Hope pushes at it with hard hands but gets an inside edge  towards short leg.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
A leading edge goes to long off, that's a rare sight! Fullish around off, Powell looks to whip it but gets a leading edge. A run taken.
Intelligent stuff from Raza. Subtle variations from him deceives Powell. Slow through the air on middle, Powell prods forward to defend but this time the ball spins away to beat him.
